title: PRD: Consumption Scenario Simulator and UX Bridge
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Summary: This PRD describes the requirements for a Consumption Scenario Simulator (the Simulator) and the UX Bridge (web/UI + SDK integration) that enable internal teams, sales, and self-serve developers to model cost/latency/fidelity trade-offs for their real workloads before committing to Dedicated or Private plans. The product ties together offline workload replay, a fidelity profile engine, a lightweight runtime emulator, and a clear UX for scenario construction and comparison.

Why this is important: Customers need a low-friction way to estimate production economics and end-user impact of changes (quantization, batching, regional routing, fallback variants, and cache policies). Existing spreadsheets and ad-hoc simulations are error-prone and siloed. A standardized Simulator improves pre-sales accuracy, reduces migration friction, and powers in-console recommendations.

Goals (measureable):
- Accuracy: Simulated token cost within ±8% of production baseline for >70% of tested workloads (see Acceptance Criteria).
- Time-to-insight: Allow a typical mid-sized customer (100k daily requests) to run a scenario and get results within 30 minutes for an up-to-10M token sample.
- Adoption: Achieve 40% usage rate by self-serve signups that run at least one simulation before moving to Dedicated within first 90 days of launch.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: workload ingestion (log/trace/SDK-based capture), scenario builder UI, fidelity profiles (quantization/variant), cost model integration, latency and tail-latency estimation, comparison reports, export to CSV/PDF, API/SDK for automation, and RBAC.
- Out of scope (MVP): full private-onprem code execution (we provide a lightweight emulator and policy configs); per-tenant legal billing changes (handled by billing team after launch).

Target users and personas:
- Self-serve developer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated economics.
- Solutions/SE pre-sales running migration estimates for enterprise customers.
- Engineering PMs and SREs wanting to validate performance of rollout policies before deployment.

Core concepts and entities:
- Workload Snapshot: sample of requests (payloads, sequence lengths, route metadata, timestamps) uploaded or captured.
- Fidelity Profile: set of model variants, quantization, and runtime optimizations (batching, cache).
- Scenario: a named configuration pairing a Workload Snapshot + Fidelity Profile + routing/region/scale assumptions.
- Simulator Run: execution of the scenario producing cost, latency distributions, and quality delta estimates.

Functional requirements:
1) Workload ingestion
   - R1.1: Accept formats: Redwood request logs (JSON lines), OpenTelemetry traces (OTLP-exported), and simple CSV (route, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms).
   - R1.2: Provide a lightweight capture SDK (Python/Node) that can capture requests to an S3-compatible staging area and scrub PII by default.
   - R1.3: Provide sample-size controls and stratified sampling by route and sequence length.

2) Fidelity/profile engine
   - R2.1: Support fidelity knobs: model variant (float16/fp16, int8, 4-bit quant), batch size, prefix-caching enabled/disabled, KV cache retention windows, and early-exit heuristics.
   - R2.2: Each fidelity knob must map to a cost delta and latency multiplier derived from the runtime profile catalog.
   - R2.3: Allow custom profiles with free-text descriptions and tags.

3) Runtime emulator and estimators
   - R3.1: Provide a lightweight emulator that can approximate per-request latency using kernelized models based on sequence length, batch shape, and chosen quantization from the runtime catalog.
   - R3.2: Estimate tail latencies (p50/p95/p99) and provide histogram + percentile output.
   - R3.3: Simulate batching effects when concurrent workloads overlap; accept concurrency/time-window assumptions.

4) Cost model integration
   - R4.1: Integrate with the existing pricing engine; cost model inputs include per-token rates per model-variant, dedicated pool holder rates, and preemptible capacity discounts.
   - R4.2: Show breakdown: per-request cost, per-token cost, infrastructure overhead, and projected monthly/annual spend under target traffic.

5) Quality delta estimation
   - R5.1: Allow users to attach a small evaluation prompt set to estimate quality deltas (e.g., for quantization or variant changes) using a fuzzy-similarity metric (ROUGE/embedding cosine).
   - R5.2: Provide a confidence band for quality metrics based on sample size and prompt diversity.

6) UX and outputs
   - R6.1: Scenario builder: step-by-step UI to create scenarios, choose snapshots, toggle fidelity knobs, and set traffic scaling assumptions.
   - R6.2: Side-by-side comparison view for up to 3 scenarios with delta highlighting (cost, latency, quality).
   - R6.3: Exportable report (PDF + CSV) that includes assumptions, raw results, and suggested migration steps.
   - R6.4: API and SDK endpoints to run scenarios programmatically and fetch simulation reports.

7) Observability and telemetry
   - R7.1: Emit telemetry for Simulator runs: duration, input size, scenario config, cost estimate, and accuracy feedback when a run is validated against production.
   - R7.2: Provide an internal dashboard for usage, top failing simulations, and accuracy drift over time.

8) Security and privacy
   - R8.1: Default PII redaction during ingestion; provide field allowlist/denylist and retention TTL configuration.
   - R8.2: RBAC: creators, viewers, org-admins. Integrate with SSO groups.

Non-functional requirements
- NFR1: Simulator service should scale to process a 10M token snapshot in under 30 minutes with default concurrency for the emulator on Redwood hosted infra.
- NFR2: 99.5% uptime for Simulator control plane (not including heavy asynchronous runs).
- NFR3: Audit logs of scenario runs retained for 180 days by default.

API and data model (surface-level)
- Endpoint: POST /api/v1/simulate 
  - Inputs: scenario_id (string), snapshot_id (string), fidelity_profile_id (string), concurrency_hint (int), time_window_ms (int)
  - Response: run_id (string), status (queued|running|completed|failed), estimated_completion_seconds (int)

- Example snapshot JSON sample (single line):
  {
    "request_id": "req-123",
    "route": "chat.default",
    "tokens_in": 26,
    "tokens_out": 128,
    "timestamp": "2027-08-15T12:03:22Z",
    "features": {"tenant_tier":"enterprise","region":"us-west-2"}
  }

UX flows and wireframe notes
- Flow A: Self-serve developer
  1. Upload snapshot or connect to captured logs.
  2. Choose baseline scenario (current hosted profile).
  3. Create scenario variant (e.g., int8, batch=32, cache=enabled).
  4. Run simulation and view side-by-side results.
  5. Export report and optionally open a ticket to sales for Dedicated sizing.

- Flow B: Solutions engineer
  1. Import customer logs via secure S3 link.
  2. Run high-fidelity profile sweep (multiple quantization + batch combos).
  3. Review quality deltas with attached prompt set.
  4. Save scenario and attach to opportunity in CRM.

Acceptance criteria
- AC1: For a curated set of 25 canonical workloads (conversational, retrieval-augmented, code-completion, short-response), Simulator cost estimate is within ±8% of production measured cost for 18/25 workloads.
- AC2: UI: user can create, run, and export a scenario within 30 minutes end-to-end for up to a 1M token snapshot.
- AC3: API: POST /api/v1/simulate returns run_id within 5s for snapshot metadata <= 100MB.
- AC4: Security: auto-redaction removes 100% of fields marked by the default denylist (emails, phone, SSN) during ingestion in 100% of test runs.

Rollout plan and milestones
- Phase 0 (MVP, 6 weeks): capture SDK + basic simulator (single fidelity profile), minimal UI to upload snapshot and run a simulation (queued).
- Phase 1 (beta, 12 weeks): fidelity engine, side-by-side comparisons, PDF export, API endpoints. Invite 10 beta customers and SEs.
- Phase 2 (GA + integrations, 20 weeks): integrate with Console recommendations, pre-sales templates, and billing signals; RBAC and SSO integration.

Ownership and stakeholders
- Product lead: Maya Chen
- Engineering owner: Arjun Patel (serving-runtime + infra integration)
- Design: Lena Rodriguez (UX flows + wireframes)
- Data/Research: Diego Morales (quality estimation models)
- Sales/SE liaison: Priya Gupta

Dependencies
- Runtime profile catalog (eng-serving-runtime) for latency/cost multipliers.
- Pricing engine and billing integration (finance).
- Console UI components (eng-developer-experience).
- S3-compatible staging and retention policy (eng-infra).

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Simulation diverges from production due to unmodeled micro-optimizations.
  - Mitigation: publish accuracy tracking and feedback loop where users can mark runs as "validated" and submit production metrics to retrain estimator.
- Risk: Customers upload sensitive data.
  - Mitigation: default redaction, clear upload UI copy, explicit confirmation for retained raw snapshots.
- Risk: Excessive compute cost for large snapshots.
  - Mitigation: provide sampling recommendations and set soft quotas for free-tier runs.

Appendix: Example CLI (capture + run)
- Capture: 
  redwood-capture --project myapp --out s3://redwood-staging/myapp-snapshots/2027-09-01.jsonl --sample-rate 0.1 

- Run: 
  curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/simulate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"snapshot_id":"s3://redwood-staging/myapp-snapshots/2027-09-01.jsonl","fidelity_profile":{"variant":"int8","batch":32,"cache":true},"concurrency_hint":50}'

Appendix: Minimal glossary
- Fidelity: The set of runtime and model choices that trade quality for cost.
- Snapshot: Sample of production-like requests used as the basis for a scenario.
- Emulator: Lightweight estimator that approximates runtime behavior without requiring full model execution.

Next steps (for reviewers)
- Confirm acceptance thresholds for cost accuracy (AC1).
- Validate sampling guidelines for large customers.
- Sign off on privacy defaults and retention TTLs.
